title: なんて, なんか and など
summary: Three small words that mean "and so on" or "things like": など is neutral, なんて and なんか add surprise or a belittling tone.

blocks.text: These three words overlap, so a dictionary list of meanings feels random. Think of them as a scale from neutral to casual.

rows: "what a ...", surprise, downplaying, a vague という

blocks.text: **など** is not a cop-out like "etc." can be in English. It lists examples and sits right after the noun, even before other particles.

blocks.jp: 机の上に本やペンなどがある。
blocks.en: On the desk there are books, pens and so on.

blocks.text: In casual speech it can also make light of a noun: the speaker rejects "things like that".

blocks.en: (I) don't say flattery or the like.

blocks.text: なんか: things like, something, somehow

なんか is a squashed 何か (something). From "something" it grows: **vague** (なんか変だ), **for some reason** (なんか眠い), and in sloppy talk a filler like "kinda". Attached to a noun it belittles it, often with real feeling, and it is common with oneself.

blocks.en: I can't stand a person like my big brother.

blocks.jp: 私なんかには無理です。
blocks.en: Someone like me can't do that.

blocks.text: なんて: a squashed なんと / 何という
なんて asks "what?" (なんて言ったの？), but it is also the exclamation **"what a ...!"**, a belittling marker after a noun, and a surprise marker after a whole clause.

blocks.jp: なんて広い部屋なんだ。

blocks.en: I hate studying and things like it.

blocks.jp: 雪が降るなんて信じられない。
blocks.en: I can't believe it's snowing! (of all things)

blocks.jp: 田中なんて人は知らない。
blocks.en: I don't know anybody called Tanaka. (and I doubt there is one)

items: **など** is neutral, **なんて** is in the middle, **なんか** is the most casual.
After a noun, なんか and なんて belittle it and replace が and を.
After a whole clause, **なんて** shows surprise or disbelief; なんか never does that.

questions.instruction: Which word is the most casual?
questions.note: なんか is the strongest and most colloquial.

questions.prompt: 机の上に本やペン＿＿がある。 (... books, pens and so on.)

options: It is very cold, and so on
questions.note: なんか = 何か, here "somehow, for some reason".

questions.instruction: Which sentence shows surprise at a whole event?
options: 雪が降るなんて信じられない。
questions.note: なんて after a clause shows surprise.

questions.instruction: What does なんて do in 勉強なんて嫌いだ?
questions.note: After a noun it makes light of it.

questions.instruction: What does なんて do in なんて広い部屋なんだ。?

questions.prompt: なんか is a squashed form of 何か.
In 私なんかには無理です, なんか shows pride.
questions.note: It belittles oneself: someone like me.

questions.instruction: Tap the word that belittles the noun
questions.note: お金なんていらない = I don't want money or such.
なんか opens the sentence as a vague "somehow".

questions.instruction: Which sentence means "I don't know anyone called Tanaka"?
options: 田中なんて人は知らない。
田中なんか人を知らなくない。
田中など人は知らなくない。

questions.instruction: Which particle disappears in 宿題など必要ない (compare 宿題は必要ない)?
questions.note: The topic は is dropped when など belittles the noun; it is not a logical particle.
